articles.title: Costco Reveals Its Full Black Friday Ad and Sale Dates for 2026
articles.summary: Costco has officially revealed its annual Holiday Savings ad and you can already start browsing what will be discounted this year. Similar to other retailers, Costco is offering multiple waves of savings leading up to Black Friday and Cyber Monday.
body: According to Costco's official page, most the deals will be available both in-warehouse or online except for on Thanksgiving and Cyber Monday. You can check out the full schedule below and click on each link to check out the ads for each sale.

The different sales have a pretty varied selection of deals, so there are savings to be had pretty much all month long. The pre-pre-Thanksgiving sale that's happening now and the pre-thanksgiving sale both have a good amount of deals on snacks, frozen foods, and kitchen essentials. There's also a decent number of discounts on TVs and gaming monitors during this time, all of which will last until Cyber Monday if they stay in stock.

As you might expect, some of the best deals on tech and other big-ticket items don't arrive until the actual Black Friday sale kicks off after Thanksgiving. This is when you'll find an RTX 5060 gaming PC for $300 off, a Dyson vacuum under $300, and a great 4K TV for under $1,000. This is also when some of the best frozen food deals happen, including $5 off Costco's signature frozen lasagnas.

articles.title: By Skipping Last-Gen Systems, Stranger Than Heaven is Allowing RGG Studio to Fully Leverage the Power of Current-Gen Consoles at Long Last
articles.summary: Stranger Than Heaven will apparently be the most technically accomplished game that developer RGG Studio has ever produced, and that’s largely due to the fact that it's being created solely for current generation hardware.
body: “We set out to make Stranger Than Heaven as a completely brand-new game, with the goal of creating something entirely fresh while putting forth the absolute best quality we can produce right now,” explained Sakamoto. “[So] we decided to drop previous-gen platforms like the PS4 and focus on creating an experience best enjoyed natively on current-gen consoles like the PS5.”

Since the launch of the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S systems back in 2020, all of RGG Studio’s games have still kept one foot stuck in the previous console generation. 2024’s Like a Dragon: Infinite Wealth was developed to run across two eras of PlayStation and Xbox, and while Xbox One was finally dropped for Yakuza Kiwami 3 & Dark Ties earlier this year, support for PlayStation 4 remained.

However, by developing Stranger Than Heaven purely for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC, the team hasn’t had to make any hardware-based compromises to its vision for the new game’s multiple decade-spanning journey through early 20th century Japan.

articles.title: 60 Years Later, the Best 'Peanuts' Quote of All Time Still Doesn't Get the Credit it Deserves
articles.summary: One of the best examples comes from a Feb. 3, 1966, comic strip in which Lucy mocks him for volunteering for a school spelling bee. Charlie Brown’s response contains some of the best advice Schulz ever put on the page. Sixty years later, it’s still something we can all stand to remember.
body: Charlie Brown has plenty of reasons to stop trying. In Charles Schulz’s Peanuts, his baseball games end in defeat, his kite gets stuck in a tree, and trusting Lucy to hold a football always ends painfully. Yet he keeps coming back. For all his worrying, Charlie Brown has a stubborn streak of hope that makes even his smallest acts of courage worth rooting for.

Schulz had announced his retirement two months earlier due to several strokes and advancing colorectal cancer, and he’d created his last strip shortly after he made the announcement. While Schulz knew he was dying, he couldn’t have known two months in advance the exact day he would die and that he’d essentially penned his own obituary by having his last comic run just one day after his death.

The timing was auspicious and perhaps even profound, which was fitting for a man with such a profound impact on American culture. Over his 50-year career, Schulz gave us nearly 18,000 Peanuts comics. Some were sweet, some were funny, and some were incredibly deep, like this one from February 3, 1966, which contains Schulz’s best-ever quote, a high bar for such a prolific talent.
points: 3, 1966, comic strip in which Lucy mocks him for volunteering for a school spelling bee.
Charlie Brown’s response contains some of the best advice Schulz ever put on the page.

articles.title: Nintendo’s Biggest Game of the Year Isn't What You Think It Is
articles.summary: This is the time of year when Nintendo's global marketing departments start limbering up and doing stretches for a big mass-market retail push. Nintendo UK launched a wholesome and emotive campaign this week, seemingly trying to one-up Nintendo Australia's legendary sad Zelda dad campaign for Tears…
body: It's been a quiet week in Switch world (give or take an Indie World showcase), sandwiched between the twin pillars of Nintendo's fall — Nintendo Switch Sports Resort and the remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Time to reflect; time to work on the timing of my table tennis backhand.

Titled "Back to Me," the ad features a despondent young student calling home; it seems like he's just been dumped. His dad invites him back for a family meal, and obviously he plays Ocarina on the train. I assumed a family session of Switch Sports Resort would feature next… but no. Instead, he and his sister make a Mii of his dad in Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream. He returns to uni, thoroughly cheered up, where he plays more Tomodachi Life with his sister over GameChat.

Tomodachi Life came out in April for the original Switch. It doesn't even have a Switch 2 Edition (yet). If Nintendo UK wanted to throw the spotlight on a game with casual appeal, GameChat support, and family avatars for their storyline, Resort was sitting right there. What gives?

articles.title: What we've been playing - "I've been intrigued by horrible images of live-action sequences for weeks"
articles.summary: Happy Halloween! Are you scared? I am: I'm in a theatre play that opens next week and we're not ready yet. I'm also off to a ghost stories evening at the theatre tonight; I've had a few people there tell me, with faces as straight as a ruler, of their eerie encounters.
body: I was in a two-hander there, a play with only two people in it, and I got to the changing room one evening to see a concerned look on the face of the other person in the show. "Have you only just got here?" he asked. "Yes," I said in response. And at this, he blanched. He's a gruff sort of fellow with a streetwise sensibility: not a person I would associate with being easily scared. But he was. "I was just talking to you," he said. "You made the curtain move as you walked past." I remember the hairs on my arms and neck standing up, and I haven't been as confident sitting in that dressing room alone since.

But back to games! This, as you know, is our regular feature where we talk about what we've been playing this week. This week, Marie cooks with Death; Connor revisits a game that terrified him as a teenager; and Bertie is a little bit disappointed by a new indie horror.

But enough about us, what about you? What have you been playing this week? Do tell all! And don't forget we have an entire archive of previous What We've Been Playings for your leisurely perusal, just in case you forgot what you were playing a year or a month or a week ago (it happens). And now onward!

articles.title: CBS's Legendary 156-Episode Sci-Fi Anthology Series is Officially Free to Watch on Streaming
articles.summary: In the realm of science fiction, Star Wars and Star Trek are generally considered to be the two biggest and most important franchises of all time. If you’re purely talking about profitability, that’s correct; those two have dominated TV and film for decades.
body: You can currently watch The Twilight Zone for free with ads on Pluto TV, Fandango, and The Roku Channel.

Debuting in 1959, The Twilight Zone ran for five seasons on CBS, totaling 156 episodes. It was created by Rod Serling, a television pioneer who sought to expand what had been seen on television throughout the 1950s, much of which was taped plays and multi-camera sitcoms like I Love Lucy. To do this, he created The Twilight Zone, a single-camera anthology series where each episode would operate like a little movie (for most of its run, the show ran for a half-hour, but season 4 tried out an hour-long format before switching back to half-hours for season 5).

While every episode of The Twilight Zone has its own characters and premise, it often explores science fiction subjects like time travel and aliens, as well as horror staples like ghosts and possessed dolls. But that was just the surface-level stuff, as many of the deeper messages in the series tackled things like prejudice, loneliness, morality, and regret.
points: In the realm of science fiction, Star Wars and Star Trek are generally considered to be the two biggest and most important franchises of all time.

articles.summary: Stranger Than Heaven, the upcoming street-brawler from the makers of Yakuza and Like a Dragon, will feature optional in-game assists to make its challenging new combat system more approachable, developer RGG Studio has confirmed to IGN in an interview conducted at Gamescom Asia x Thailand Game Show…
body: In IGN’s most recent hands-on with the game, my colleague Michael Higham described Stranger Than Heaven’s parry-based combat system as “demanding”, adding that “you really have to pay attention to attack animations not just for timing, but to make the correct call on the direction it's coming from.” This initially seemed like it could prove to be divisive among fans of the comparatively carefree button-mashing combo systems found in RRG Studios’ previous adventures like Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii and Lost Judgment, but it turns out that Stranger Than Heaven’s more complex combat system will only be as difficult as players want it to be.

While that’s certainly the only big game coming to Series X, the first few weeks of November are deceptively crowded.
body: These are just five of the games you can look forward to in November. Yes, the list includes the big one, but there’s more to check out than you might think. If you’re not interested in going on an open-world crime spree, you’ll still have some solid options this month.

Though Xbox Game Pass isn’t getting any major tentpole releases in November, it is adding a lot of promising smaller games. Chief among them is Gravhounds, a new co-op shooter where you shoot aliens and build a base together. Sounds simple enough, but there’s one eye-catching twist: You play as a pack of humanoid dogs. Gravhounds has a real “WTF” factor that made it a standout game during this year’s Gamescom, so we’ll be curious to see if the shooting holds up to the wacky visuals.

articles.title: EA Just Shelved A Mysterious Sims Project—That Could Be Good News For Players
articles.summary: It's been another rough year for video games, with countless studio closures, staff layoffs, and projects that barely managed to even get off the ground before they were unceremoniously cut short.
body: This was especially painful for Mass Effect players, who were looking forward to the upcoming Mass Effect 5, which we now know was tentatively titled Mass Effect: Universe. But it's not just BioWare fans who are upset at the moment. Fans of EA's other properties are growing increasingly concerned about the future of those franchises, if any future is planned for them at all. My colleague Levi Winslow recently wrote about their concerns for the Skate franchise in the wake of layoffs at its development studio. Meanwhile, I'm quite worried about the fate of The Sims.

In the same breath it announced the end of BioWare, EA also reaffirmed its commitment to Apex Legends, Skate, and The Sims franchises. But everyone knows that when it comes to profits, EA's sports titles outrun its other IPs by a country mile. If EA is willing to pull the plug on legacy franchises like Mass Effect and Dragon Age, where does that leave its other franchises, like The Sims 4?
points: It's been another rough year for video games, with countless studio closures, staff layoffs, and projects that barely managed to even get off the ground before they were unceremoniously cut short.

articles.title: CoD: Modern Warfare To Cut Real-Life Korean Tragedy Segment After Backlash
articles.summary: Publisher Activision has responded to criticism over using a devastating tragedy in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, saying that the incident will be removed from the military shooter in a November 12 update. The Seoul Halloween crowd crush occurred in October 2022 in Itaewon.
body: "Using such an incident as material for a game intended for entertainment purposes is itself highly inappropriate and a senseless act," the groups said, according to the BBC. "The Itaewon tragedy was a tragic disaster that produced hundreds of casualties, and citizens who participated in the rescue efforts or witnessed the event at the time continue to suffer from trauma. If the game developer has even a minimum level of courtesy and empathy toward the victims, they should promptly take corrective measures."

Activision has heard the call and plans to remove the depiction from Modern Warfare 4 when an update arrives on November 12. In responding to the criticism, Activision said it never intended to trivialize the disaster or make light of human suffering.

"In developing Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, we approached the subject matter with care and respect. The game’s opening cinematic utilises some real-world news coverage to establish the game’s fictional narrative," Activision said. "It is not intended to reference or trivialise the Itaewon disaster or any other real-world tragedy in any way, shape or form."

articles.title: GOTY hopeful Mina the Hollower bought the studio financial stability "for now," while the Shovel Knight devs work on a new 3D game
articles.summary: Yacht Club Games has confirmed that most of its developers are now working on a brand new 3D game (potentially Shovel Knight 3D), after the critically-acclaimed Mina the Hollower did well enough for the team to continue.
body: Before launching its old-school adventure game earlier this year, Yacht Club described Mina the Hollower as a "make-or-break" moment for the beloved indie studio. A global pandemic and a failed experiment to turn Yacht Club into a multi-project studio had left the developer on thin ice, it seems.

But Mina the Hollower sold well enough to buy the studio more time, according to a new Reddit AMA full of interesting tidbits. Asked if Mina was able to secure financial stability for the company, Sean Velasco simply said "yes… for now!" Mina managed to sell over 500,000 copies in its first two weeks, so it's well on its way to the one million copies the devs were once hoping for.

For the foreseeable future, the devs aren't ready to talk about the kinds of DLC and spin-offs and follow-ups that dear old Shovel Knight enjoyed for many years, but they're not abandoning their newest baby either. "We're working on more post-release features," the devs wrote, which includes "expanded randomizer options, enemy and boss randomization, more modifiers, speedrunner features" and more ways "to do even more in Mina."

articles.title: New Assassin’s Creed Game Is Out Now, If You Don’t Mind Being Board
articles.summary: If you thought there wasn't going to be a new Assassin's Creed game this year, think again. It's not a video game, but Assassin's Creed: Animus is out today, turning the series into an adventure-style board game for 1-4 players.
body: A competitive game that pits players against each other as they explore distinct eras from the video games, Assassin's Creed: Animus features four protagonists to choose from in its standard edition: Eivor, Ezio, Altair, and Connor. The Collector's Edition, meanwhile, expands to 10 eras and features 16 protagonists, adding game characters like Edward Kenway, Jacob and Evie Frye, and Kassandra.

You and up to three of your friends (or you alone) work to complete objectives across these eras, taking down assassination targets in the way you see fit via "memory blocks." Whether you go in with your sword drawn or engage in a sneakier approach is up to you.

The standard version of Assassin's Creed: Animus is available to order now for $65, while the limited Collector's Edition costs $229. Alongside the extra characters and eras, this version comes with a storage box, acrylic tokens, a metal Piece of Eden, a cloth token bag, "special event cards," and an Animus Card Holder.

articles.title: What are we all playing this weekend?
articles.summary: My scares should have been reserved for today, what with it being All Hallows' Eve and all, but my fright came on Thursday.
body: I unlocked my front door and started up the internal staircase to the kitchen, not even bothering to turn on the lights. Out of the dark, something jumped down the stairs at me, hitting me in the stomach. I flicked the lights on in a panic and saw a small brown thing with a long tail bolting back up the staircase. A mouse. In my house.
Terrifying stuff, I'm sure you will agree. It almost put me off my risotto. Anyway, this is what the rest of the team will be up to this weekend..

Ollie I've settled into a very comfy rhythm of playing the latest Trackmania campaign and also a bit of Factorio, both with my brother. When I've a bit of time to myself I'm also interested in trying out Queen's Domain. Heard good things!

videos.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 DMZ Review
videos.summary: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's DMZ mode reviewed by Jarrett Green on PlayStation 5, also available on Xbox Series X|S, Nintendo Switch 2, and PC.
body: "Modern Warfare 4’s DMZ mode finally puts the fun and frantic gunplay signature to Call of Duty into a genre I fancy more than its typical PvP multiplayer. While executing missions, the semi-arcadey running and gunning mixes nicely with the vibrant exploration elements in Hajin and the rapid fire Dynamic Objectives and side ops, creating a delightfully high-tension experience that also doesn’t get too sweaty. All of the other things around it – crafting, gunsmithing, and to a larger extent the almost RPG-like skill trees for individual operators – provide little incentive to engage with them all that rigorously. This may not bode well for DMZ’s staying power as a “service” across the coming year, but in the present, it’s a strong addition to the growing list of worthwhile extraction shooters."
points: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's DMZ mode reviewed by Jarrett Green on PlayStation 5, also available on Xbox Series X|S, Nintendo Switch 2, and PC.

videos.summary: A new report from Bloomberg claims EA had to choose between Star Wars and Mass Effect, which resulted in the closure of BioWare. EA is facing financial pressure due to the $18 billion debt it took on during the Saudi buyout.
points: A new report from Bloomberg claims EA had to choose between Star Wars and Mass Effect, which resulted in the closure of BioWare.
EA is facing financial pressure due to the $18 billion debt it took on during the Saudi buyout.
The company then only had enough budget to back one big sci-fi game, and they chose Star Wars Battlefront 3 as the safer bet.
In other news, Gears of War: E-Day has moved only 400,000 copies across Xbox and PC, a relatively low number for a marquee franchise.
